newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit little changed despite trade surplus.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit little changed despite trade surplus.

text.p: Corporate demand for dollars blocked the ringgit's rise despite positive Malaysia's trade data, dealers said.
The ringgit stayed within tight ranges all day after failing to break 2.4920 soon after the release of June trade figures, which showed a 574 million ringgit surplus.
"There's corporate demand at 2.4920. The market tried to push dollar down but failed," said a Singapore-based dealer.
At 0900 GMT, ringgit was at 2.4930/35 per dollar against 2.4928/38 at close of local trading on Monday.

In the longer term, dealers and economists said the positive trade balance trend will underpin the ringgit. "All in all, it should provide some bullish trend for investors to come back to Malaysia," said Jimmy Koh, an economist at I.D.E.A.
Dollar/ringgit is expected to head higher in the immediate term after the market noted the strong support at 2.4920, dealers said.

In the money market, interbank rates were softer after surging recently following interventions by Bank Negara last week to tighten liquidity. The one-month rate was at 7.20 percent from 7.30. -- Reme Ahmad (603-201 4813)
